_comment: Example structural gate config, written for a plan document. Every check here is one where the check IS the thing meant - no proxy in between. Copy, edit, delete what doesn't apply. Keys beginning with underscore are ignored.
_required_sections: Headings that must exist AND have a non-empty body. Case-insensitive. Catches the silent-omission failure: the section that was supposed to be there and just isn't. A section that may legitimately be empty should say 'none' rather than be blank.
_max_words: A length cap is not a proxy for quality when the rule literally is a length. Leave it out unless the user has asked for one.
_required_phrases: Text that must appear verbatim. Use for a status line, a required license header, a mandated disclaimer.
_forbidden_phrases: Phrases that must not appear anywhere. Placeholder text is the usual case: it survives review because a reader skims past it.
_section_forbidden_phrases: Phrases allowed in the document but not under one heading. Use when a correction keeps recurring because something lands in the wrong section - here, evidence that can only be gathered on another machine being written as a pre-acceptance gate.
_define_before_use: Terms whose first appearance must be inside the definition section. Catches the ordering failure that a mere presence check misses - a glossary at the end of the document does not help the reader who needed it on page one.
_companion_files: Files that must exist alongside the artifact. They get forgotten, and their absence is invisible until someone needs one.
_rejected: These keys are refused by validate_artifact.py on purpose: max_grade_level, reading_level, flesch_kincaid, max_sentence_words, vocabulary_difficulty. All are proxies. Blocking on them teaches sentence-chopping, which strips connectives and can make text score easier while reading harder. Run scan_prose.py for those signals instead - advisory, located, unscored.
